articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker Cost Just $40 Million to Develop
articles.summary: Developer Rebel Wolves' September success story, The Blood of Dawnwalker, cost just $40 million to make. Information related to the Warsaw, Poland-based studio's behind-the-scenes activities comes from a new Bloomberg report.
body: Game designer Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, who previously served as one of the leading developers behind games like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt and Cyberpunk 2077, worked on early versions of Rebel Wolves' first game with a small team back in 2022. Tomaszkiewicz self-funded the project for that first year as the team hammered out its prototype in hopes of finding a partner, with NetEase later stepping in with the fund the game while acquiring 26% of the studio.

The $40 million figure comfortably lands The Blood of Dawnwalker in the AA space instead of the AAA realm where games often carry heftier price tags. For comparison, IO Interactive's 007 First Light reportedly carried a budget of more than $200 million. Sony's struggling Marathon game is said to have had a similar budget, with games like The Last of Us Part 2 and Horizon Forbidden West also reportedly in that range.
points: Developer Rebel Wolves' September success story, The Blood of Dawnwalker, cost just $40 million to make.

articles.title: The Witch Hat Atelier Manga Box Set Gets a Major Price Cut at Amazon Ahead of Season 2
articles.summary: Witch Hat Atelier is my favorite new anime series of 2026. It's beautifully animated, features a unique magic system, and even has dubbing that elevates the world-building. If you haven't already seen it, I highly recommend grabbing a Crunchyroll subscription to stream all 13 episodes.
body: Like any popular anime series, however, Witch Hat Atelier got its start as a really popular manga series. The art style of Kamome Shirahama is absolutely stunning and blends classic manga techniques with modern comic book illustration. If you've never read manga before, this is a great place to start. And with the most recent discount at Amazon, now is a good time to snag the first six volumes for cheap.

The first Witch Hat Atelier box set includes the first six volumes, which is only a portion of the ongoing series. There are currently only 14 volumes available in English, so this set collects almost half of what's available right now.

For those who have already seen the anime, you should already be familiar with the content of the first four volumes. Episode 13 concluded the first season by adapting the story up through the end of volume 4, meaning volumes 5 and 6 will continue the story where the show left off. Like any adaptation, there are plenty of extras you'll get to experience by reading the manga that wasn't shown in the anime.
points: Witch Hat Atelier is my favorite new anime series of 2026.
It's beautifully animated, features a unique magic system, and even has dubbing that elevates the world-building.

articles.title: New Pokemon Plane Looks Incredible, Even Includes Themed Cups And Napkins
articles.summary: Japanese airline All Nippon Airways (ANA) has unveiled a Pokemon-themed airliner to celebrate the franchise's 30th anniversary this year, and it looks incredible. The Green Pokemon Jet, as it's called, made its inaugural flight from Haneda to Honolulu today following a big unveiling event--you can…
body: Inside the aircraft, there are headrest covers, paper cups, and napkins containing Pokemon branding. Beyond that, people flying on it can watch and listen to Pokemon-themed in-flight entertainment, including Pokemon: The First Movie and the best-of soundtrack from the show (1997-2023).
In addition to Haneda, which is the busiest airport in Japan, the Pokemon plane will make stops at a variety of airports in Okinawa, Kyushu, and Shikoku.

Pokemon was created in Japan, and this is not the first time we've seen a Pokemon plane. All the way back in 2000, Japan Airlines announced that its fleet of jets would include Pokemon characters printed on the sides for domestic flights, along with Pokemon-themed in-flight entertainment.
In 2024, ANA created a Pokemon-themed safety video, featuring the franchise's adorable little monsters teaching passengers how to stay safe during flights.

articles.title: Remedy Honors the Late David Lynch in Control Resonant With Powerful Twin Peaks Quote
articles.summary: Remedy Entertainment's games have always been inspired by the late, great filmmaker David Lynch, who passed away in January 2025. Best known for the influential muder mystery series Twin Peaks and cult classic thriller Mulholland Drive, Lynch's penchant for merging surrealism with horror and…
body: Throughout the open zones in Control Resonant, you'll find tons of details in the environment that build up its fictional version of New York City. One is a movie theater with a marquee outside that reads: "NOW PLAYING: FIX YOUR HEART OR DIE."

"When I had you working undercover at the DEA, you were a confused and wild thing sometimes. I had enough dirt on you to fill the Grand Canyon. And I never used a spoonful because you were and are a great agent. And when you became Denise, I told all your colleagues, those clown comics, to fix their hearts or die."

Thus, the phrase "fix your heart or die" had become an iconic line not only in the Twin Peaks pantheon, highlighting the convictions of Lynch's character, but also a motto and rallying cry for transgender folks and in trans rights activism.

Bryson's depictation in the totality of Twin Peaks isn't without its problematic tropes, especially in the original 1990-1991 run, but Lynch's character (and Lynch himself) made it a point to make a statement against transphobia outright. And that resonated with many trans people.

articles.title: This Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Hardcover Might Be DC's Most Exciting Release of 2027
articles.summary: DC Comics has released its full list of solicitations for December 2026. And while there's a lot to be excited for at the end of the year (including the impending finale of Tom King and Daniel Sampere's Wonder Woman run), the biggest news involves a new hardcover collection of Alan Moore's classic…
body: The Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Omnibus promises to be the definitive collection of what most would regard as one of the finest comics ever published by DC. That's because this two-volume slipcase set will reprint the entirety of Moore's run with a restored and remastered version of the original coloring and period-appropriate paper stock.

For those not familiar, there are currently two ways of reading Moore's Swamp Thing in collected format, neither of which feature the original coloring from the single issues. The six trade paperbacks and two Absolute Edition hardcovers each have new, modernized coloring, and both versions have been heavily criticized by fans for altering the tone of the original comics.

You can check out this Reddit thread to see a side-by-side comparison of the originals, the trade paperbacks, and the Absolute Editions. The differences are pretty stark, to put it mildly. DC hasn't yet released any interior preview art of the Swamp Thing by Alan Moore Omnibus, but the expectation is that the books will be much more in line with how the series originally appeared in the '80s.

articles.title: I Guess I’ll Delete Every PS5 Game I Own To Make Room For FF7 Revelation
articles.summary: There are quite a few months until Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches on Nintendo Switch 2, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. But you're going to want to get your systems ready now because the download for the final showdown between Cloud and Sephiroth may be big.
body: According to a September 18 VGC Interview with game director Naoki Hamaguchi, the file size for Revelation will "probably" be absolutely massive. So huge, in fact, that Hamaguchi acknowledged that there was no way the game would fit on one--or even two or three--discs.

"In a word, yes. Things are still getting worked out, but it's probably going to be around 200GB of game," Hamaguchi said. "I understand there are a lot of opinions about this topic, but at the end of the day, the fact is we need to overcome the hardware to a certain extent."

2OOGB is pretty huge, especially when the base PS5 (which is what I still have, sue me) holds approximately 667GB of usable storage space. With many of the games I own clocking in just at or well over 100GB (like The Elder Scrolls Online, Ghost of Yotei, Infinity Nikki, and Mortal Shell 2), I'm already debating with myself what games I delete to make room for Cloud's big sword and Sephiroth's shampoo collection.

articles.title: Ex-Naughty Dog Dev Apologizes To God Of War Studio For What He Said About Laufey
articles.summary: Bruce Straley, best known for his work at Naughty Dog on the Uncharted and The Last of Us franchises, has apologized to God of War: Laufey studio Santa Monica Studio, after he said he was "not excited" about what the game was offering, at least in some respects.
body: Straley told Edge that he thinks "every pixel" in Laufey looks "mindblowing and that he is "blown away" by the lengths Santa Monica Studio went to. However, Straley said he is "not excited" by "what you're doing in the game."
Beyond Laufey, Straley said he feels there is "no opportunity to inject fresh, innovative ideas" in AAA games generally.

In a new statement shared on social media, Straley said, "I want to apologize to the Laufey team for dragging you all into this uninvited and unnecessary negative attention." He said he was trying to make a point about his concerns about the AAA games industry generally, and acknowledged that he made a mistake by naming Laufey specifically.

"I have thoughts about what’s wrong & the possible serious harm done to our industry & how we might be able to fix it. But in trying to have a thoughtful conversation I stuck my foot in my mouth & mentioned Laufey, and that was my mistake," he said.

articles.title: Should you skip the War Arc (Act 2) in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave?
articles.summary: You can skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, but while it's not necessarily the best choice, it's not a terrible one either. Whether it's the right one for you depends on where you're at in the game and what you're hoping to get from this part of it.
body: Below, we explain whether you should skip the War Arc in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

If this is your first time playing through Fortune's Weave, then no, you absolutely should not skip the War Arc at the obelisk. It's an essential bridge connecting the end of the Flame Lords' first acts to Act 3. It's important even if you aren't interested in the story, too, since it gets you ready to face the much steeper challenges Act 3 throws at you. The battles become bigger and more demanding from here on out.

After that, it depends on what you're doing. The maps and story in Act 2 are the same for every character, except for a unique scene at the start and very end. You aren't missing anything there if you skip.

articles.title: Where to find wonder leaves in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: Wonder leaves are common materials you can find in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. You need one of these plants to complete one of Leda's perform quests called "Elegant Drink Recipes." To collect plants in the game, you need to visit specific nodes on the world map and use the command "Search," but…
body: If you need help locating this material, here's where you can find wonder leaves in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

The only place where you can find wonder leaves is in the Mahapira Garden node in Ogmios region, on the extreme south part of the map. After you have opened the map and reached Theodora's hometown, Megaira, keep going east. Pass the Grania Stronghold and keep heading east until you reach the Fort Zanbar node. From there, go north, heading to the further tip of the shore to find the Mahapira Garden.

The fastest way to get to the Ogmios region is by using the carriage and traveling to the Salacia Posthouse. Your second option, in case you have unlocked Theodora's ships, is to sail south, but this method requires too many turns, and it's only reasonable if you have many days to spare in a chapter. Besides, Ogmios is a late game area, and you should be around level 35 to explore it while in Part 1 of the game.

articles.title: Classes and unlock requirements in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave classes work a bit differently than you might be used to if you played Three Houses. They come in several tiers, similar to Three Houses, but some of the intermediate classes only unlock if you meet certain conditions.
body: Below, we list Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's classes and how to unlock them. This is an in-progress guide, as we're still missing a few master-tier and divine-tier classes. However, those are unavailable until Act 3, so you won't have to do anything to get them until then.

Every character starts in a beginner class, either commoner or noble, and gets a helpful little class mastery skill. After that, it's time to change to something more specialized. A new tier of classes unlocks when you reach certain renown thresholds, and you'll need to purchase certifications to take that class' exam. The game autosaves before you see the exam result, so there's no chance of cheesing it and retaking the exam until you pass.

The better option is to just hold off taking an exam until your character has at least a 75% chance of passing or higher. Skill rank matters here, but level matters even more. If you need to be level 35, for example, but you take the exam at level 32 with the right skill ranks, you'll still end up with a low chance of passing.

articles.title: Sony execs behind iconic game-sharing meme recreate it, but fittingly, without a physical game
articles.summary: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic "this is how you share your games on PS4" moment - now with a very timely game-less picture.
body: No matter which side of the console war you sat on in 2013, there's a good chance Sony's 'Used Game Instructional Video' reached you. In the months leading up to the launch of the PS4 and Xbox One, Microsoft's restrictive game-sharing plans became hugely controversial and Sony decided to take advantage of the negative fan frenzy with one short clip.

PlayStation's president of first-party studios, Shuhei Yoshida, and head of third-party relations, Adam Boyes, stood in front of a camera and explained to folks how game-sharing worked on the company's then-next-gen console. Step one? Yoshida handed Boyes a physical copy of Killzone: Shadow Fall. Step two? There was none. That was all. The video racked up 21m views in the past 13 years and has since become one of the defining moments of the PS4's launch.

Now, Yoshida shared that he reunited with Boyes while at Tokyo Game Show 2026 in a new online post. "Met with a best friend," he wrote, alongside a picture of the duo recreating their famous game-sharing pose. Quite fittingly, neither have a physical game to share.
points: Former PlayStation executives Shuhei Yoshida and Adam Boyes have recreated their iconic "this is how you share your games on PS4" moment - now with a very timely game-less picture.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave Is Way Easier If You Play a Second Route
articles.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave lets you clear the whole game by playing just one route — or none at all if you're a real sicko and ignore the Flame Lords. But you really, really should do at least two routes before tackling the final campaign against Balor.
body: And you shouldn't start it until you finish at least one extra route.
In short, yes, you should definitely play a second route in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave.

Whoever you pick first, you'll be up against it in terms of money, renown, and balancing free time with exploring the map to find better weapons and gifts. Some characters can get more money or renown than others thanks to their unique subquests, but regardless, the number of quests in each chapter is limited. Every character has a handful of potential allies they can recruit at a lower level of renown, but "handful" is the operative word there. The rest require a renown level of seven or higher.

Act 2 expands the number of characters you can deploy in each mission to 15. It does supply a few of them if you don't have enough, but these are guest units, and as such, you have no control over their equipment and class. And sure, you can go up against the seemingly endless horde of foes that act throws at you, though having 12 to 15 characters makes managing the pressure much easier.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave lets you clear the whole game by playing just one route — or none at all if you're a real sicko and ignore the Flame Lords.

articles.title: Despite controversial reviews and online mockery, Marvel's Wolverine looks to have sold 1.9m on PS5 - and over 1 in 5 sales are physical
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine has been in the hot seat over the last week or so, but mixed reviews and internet memes seemingly haven't put a dent in the superhero game's adamantium frame.
body: Alinea Analytics' Rhys Elliot today reported that Marvel's Wolverine has moved around 1.9m copies in its first three days and, thus, dropped a fat bag of cash into PlayStation's lap. The figure apparently includes a million copies that came from pre-launch digital pre-orders. Altogether, the divisive action game's made upwards of $130m so far.

While Sony itself plans on ending production of discs for new PlayStation games in 2028, there seems to be plenty of demand for physical versions of its new blockbuster. According to the report, 22.9% of sales came from physical editions.

Interestingly, Marvel's Wolverine's physical-to-digital ratio is slightly heavier on the digital side than some of the PS5's other big hitters. A previous Alinea Analytics report claimed Insomniac Games' last superpowered romp, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, made 35% of its PS5 revenue from physical sales. Around 46% of Astro Bot 's sales also came from disc-based copies, while Ghost of Yotei 's physical split was 37.6%.
Keep in mind, Marvel's Wolverine hasn't been on store shelves for very long at all and the holiday season could well make a difference in that percentage split over the coming weeks and months.

videos.title: PlayStation’s Creative Future Has Never Looked Bleaker
videos.summary: Cutting ties with Kojima and poor Wolverine reviews are just the latest issues in a difficult generation for PlayStation. The platform's creartive future has never looked bleaker.
body: It’s impossible to know how PlayStation bosses felt after seeing many critics walk away from Insomniac’s Wolverine with an apathetic shrug. A sub-80 on Metacritic is infamously considered a disaster in the triple-A space, and so Sony certainly won’t be thrilled, but it would be easy for the company to brush this away as an uncharacteristic miss. However, that would require wilfully ignoring the sad reality that PlayStation Studios is currently far from fertile ground for single-player adventures.

Never has it been clearer that PlayStation Studios needs to find the next evolutionary stage of the “traditional” video game. Never has it been clearer that it needs its next Metal Gear Solid, the revolutionary Hideo Kojima game that defined what we could expect from PlayStation back in 1998.
points: Cutting ties with Kojima and poor Wolverine reviews are just the latest issues in a difficult generation for PlayStation.
The platform's creartive future has never looked bleaker.
It’s impossible to know how PlayStation bosses felt after seeing many critics walk away from Insomniac’s Wolverine with an apathetic shrug.
Never has it been clearer that it needs its next Metal Gear Solid, the revolutionary Hideo Kojima game that defined what we could expect from PlayStation back in 1998.
